items.prompt:
Read this paragraph. Identify the off-topic sentence AND rewrite the paragraph without it, adding one stronger detail to any existing sentence.

'Frogs are interesting animals. They begin life as tadpoles in the water. My teacher has a frog poster in our classroom. As they grow, frogs develop legs and leave the water. Adult frogs can live on both land and in water.'
items.answer: Off-topic sentence: 'My teacher has a frog poster in our classroom.' Revised paragraph: 'Frogs are fascinating amphibians with an amazing life cycle. They begin life as tadpoles in the water, swimming with a long tail and no legs. As they grow, frogs develop powerful legs and their tail disappears. Adult frogs can live on both land and in water, making them one of nature's most adaptable creatures.'

steps: Remove the off-topic sentence.
Add a specific detail to one sentence to strengthen the paragraph.

items.prompt:
Read this weak paragraph and identify THREE specific things that need revising. Then write your improved version.

'Books are good. I like reading. Books have pictures sometimes. Reading is important.'
items.answer: Problems: (1) Too vague — no specific reasons or details. (2) No linking words in the second and third sentences. (3) No strong concluding sentence. Improved: 'Books are one of the best ways to learn and explore new worlds. I love reading because every book takes me on a different adventure, from space travel to jungle mysteries. Books can have beautiful illustrations that bring the story to life, or just words that let your imagination paint the pictures. Reading every day helps your brain grow stronger and prepares you for everything you will do in life.'

steps: Vagueness: add specific reasons and examples.
No linking words: add 'because,' 'from,' 'or.'
No concluding sentence: add one that wraps up the paragraph.

items.prompt: A student wrote this opinion piece introduction: 'I think recess is good. Recess is nice. Recess is my favorite part of school.' Revise the introduction to make it stronger. Replace vague words with specific details and combine or rewrite sentences as needed.
items.answer: Revised: 'I believe recess is one of the most important parts of the school day. Running, jumping, and playing outside gives students the energy and focus they need to learn well when they come back inside.'

steps: Eliminate vague words ('good,' 'nice,' 'favorite') and replace with specific claims.
Combine ideas into fewer, more powerful sentences.
A strong introduction states the opinion and hints at a reason.

items.prompt:
Read this narrative. Which detail, if added after the second sentence, would make it MOST vivid?

'Last fall, my class planted a garden. We dug small holes in the soil. ___ Over the next few weeks, we watered the seeds every day.'

A) 'Gardening is an outdoor activity.'
B) 'Each of us planted three seeds and patted the cool, crumbly dirt gently over the top.'
C) 'My grandma has a garden too.'
D) 'Seeds can grow into many different plants.'
items.answer: B — it adds a specific, sensory action that shows exactly what the students did.

steps: The paragraph is describing the students planting a garden. Option B adds specific physical details (three seeds, cool crumbly dirt) that match the scene.

items.prompt:
Revise this weak informative paragraph by (1) strengthening the vague introduction, (2) adding one more specific fact, and (3) writing a stronger concluding sentence.

'Weather is the thing outside. It can be sunny or rainy. Weather can be cold or hot. Weather is important.'
items.answer: Revised: 'Weather is the condition of the atmosphere outside, including temperature, wind, and precipitation. It can be sunny and warm, or cold and rainy — sometimes changing several times in a single day. Severe weather events like thunderstorms, blizzards, and hurricanes can affect transportation, farming, and safety across large regions. Understanding weather helps scientists predict dangerous storms and helps people plan and prepare for all kinds of conditions.'

steps: Introduction: replace vague description with a definition.
Add a specific fact about severe weather.
Concluding sentence: explain why understanding weather matters.

items.prompt: A student peer-reviewed her classmate's narrative and wrote: 'Your story needs more details.' Is this helpful feedback? What would be MORE helpful to say? Write an example of specific revision feedback for this sentence: 'I felt bad when I missed the goal.'
items.answer: 'Your story needs more details' is not very helpful because it does not tell the writer WHAT to add or WHERE. More helpful feedback: 'In the sentence about missing the goal, could you tell us what it felt like in your body — did your stomach drop? Did you feel heat in your face? Adding those feelings would make the moment much more real for the reader.'

steps: Helpful revision feedback is specific: it names the exact sentence or part and tells the writer what kind of detail to add.
General comments like 'needs more details' do not guide the writer.

items.prompt:
Read this informative paragraph. There are two problems: one off-topic sentence and one vague sentence. Identify both and write the corrected version.

'Penguins are birds that live in cold places. They cannot fly, but they are great swimmers. I have seen a penguin movie three times. Penguins eat fish and other sea animals. Penguins are neat.'
items.answer: Off-topic: 'I have seen a penguin movie three times.' Vague: 'Penguins are neat.' Corrected: 'Penguins are flightless birds that live in some of the coldest regions on Earth, including Antarctica. Although they cannot fly, penguins are remarkable swimmers who use their flipper-like wings to glide through the ocean at up to 15 miles per hour. They hunt fish, squid, and tiny crustaceans called krill to survive. Penguins are extraordinary animals, perfectly adapted to thrive in one of the harshest environments on the planet.'

steps: Remove 'I have seen a penguin movie three times' (off-topic).
Replace 'Penguins are neat' with a strong, specific concluding sentence.

items.prompt: What is the difference between revising and editing? Write one example of a revision task and one example of an editing task for this sentence: 'i saw a really big dog yesterday'
items.answer: Revising = improving content and ideas. Editing = fixing mechanical errors. Revision task: Add specific details ('I saw a massive, shaggy Saint Bernard charging toward me down the sidewalk yesterday'). Editing task: Capitalize 'I' and 'I saw,' and add a period at the end.

steps: Revise = make the content stronger (add who, what, how big, what happened).
Edit = fix the lowercase 'i,' and add a period.

items.prompt: A student's narrative ending reads: 'It was fun. We went home.' Revise it into a strong 2-sentence ending. The story was about visiting a grandfather who lives on a farm.
items.answer: Sample: 'As the truck pulled away from Grandpa's farm, I pressed my face to the cold window and watched the red barn grow smaller and smaller until it disappeared around the bend. I already knew that this summer visit had carved itself into the part of my memory where the best things live.'

steps: Ending 1: describe the moment of leaving with a vivid sensory detail.
Ending 2: add a reflection on what the visit meant.

items.prompt:
Read this opinion paragraph. The student was told to 'focus on the topic.' Which sentence does NOT focus on the topic, and why?

'I believe students should read for fun every day. Reading is great because it improves vocabulary and makes you a stronger writer. My school has a big cafeteria. Also, reading for fun helps students relax and reduces stress after a busy school day.'
items.answer: 'My school has a big cafeteria' does not focus on the topic (reading for fun). It is a random fact about the school that has nothing to do with why students should read.

steps: Focus means every sentence connects directly to the main idea. A cafeteria is unrelated to reading benefits.

items.prompt:
Revise this paragraph to improve THREE things: the vague introduction, the missing reason in sentence 2, and the weak concluding sentence.

'Art class is great. It is fun for kids. We also get to make stuff. Art is nice.'
items.answer: Revised: 'Art class is one of the most valuable parts of the school day. It is especially fun because students get to express their creativity and make something original that did not exist before. We also get to learn about famous artists, explore different materials like paint and clay, and work together on big projects. Art teaches skills like patience, creativity, and attention to detail that students carry with them for the rest of their lives.'

steps: Intro: replace 'Art class is great' with a stronger claim.
Reason: add 'because' to the second sentence.
Concluding sentence: replace 'Art is nice' with a statement of value and impact.

items.prompt: A classmate says: 'I never need to revise — my first draft is always good.' Do you agree? Write 2-3 sentences explaining why revising is important, using examples.
items.answer: Sample: Revising is important because even the best writers look back at their work and find ways to make it stronger. For example, your first draft might have a vague sentence like 'It was fun,' which revision could turn into a vivid detail like 'We laughed so hard that tears rolled down our cheeks.' Without revising, you miss the chance to make your writing the best it can be.

steps: Explain that first drafts are just the beginning.
Give a concrete example of how revising changes a vague sentence into a strong one.

items.prompt:
Read this informative paragraph. A teacher says: 'Add a detail to your second sentence to make it stronger.' Write the improved second sentence.

Original second sentence: 'The Amazon River is very long.'
items.answer: Sample improved sentence: 'The Amazon River stretches over 4,000 miles through the South American rainforest, making it one of the longest rivers in the world.'

steps: Add specific information: HOW long? Where is it? What makes it notable?

items.prompt:
Read this narrative paragraph. Which revision would make the MOST improvement?

'We went camping. It rained. We stayed in the tent. Then it stopped raining and we had fun.'

A) Change 'camping' to 'a camping trip.'
B) Add temporal words and specific sensory details to each sentence.
C) Add a second paragraph about cooking breakfast.
D) Remove the sentence about rain.
items.answer: B — adding temporal words and sensory details would transform the vague sentences into a vivid narrative. This addresses the biggest weakness: lack of specific details and narrative flow.

steps: A is a minor change.
C adds content but does not fix the existing vague sentences.
D removes relevant content.
B is the most impactful revision.

items.prompt:
Revise this complete opinion paragraph to strengthen it. Identify each weakness and fix it.

'I think art is important. Art helps people. Art makes things look nice. Art is my favorite subject. I think art matters a lot.'
items.answer: Weaknesses: vague reasons ('helps people,' 'look nice'), the personal opinion 'my favorite subject' interrupts the argument, and the ending repeats the opening. Revised: 'I believe art is one of the most important subjects in school. Art helps people express emotions and ideas that words alone cannot capture, giving a voice to feelings that might otherwise stay hidden. Art also trains the eye to notice beauty, detail, and creativity in the everyday world. For these reasons, I believe art education deserves as much attention as reading or math.'

steps: Replace vague reasons with specific ones using 'because.'
Remove or redirect 'my favorite subject' so it does not interrupt the argument.
Replace the repeated ending with a strong, distinct concluding sentence.
